cultural.vision_reason: A striped indigo-and-white handwoven cotton tobe (boubou) with hand-embroidered decorative panel, a classic men's gown form associated with Wolof and neighboring West African weaving traditions; consistent with the claimed ethnicity and category.

physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Man’s robe (tobe, boubou), tailored from 15 strips of handspun indigo and white cotton, hand-woven and hand-sewn together. The strips continue over the shoulders on both sides of the gown, with a hole left in the centre for the head, and the edges have been tailored to form arm-holes. The six strips on the outside alternate two patterns: one of light indigo, the other of dark indigo along which white lines have been embroidered. The central three strips are of dark indigo, and have been extensively hand-embroidered on both front and back with patterns in red, brown, blue and white thread. A pocket has been sewn on the front, which is also heavily embroidered with squares, spirals and fans. Two strips cut from imported red cloth in an S and backward C shape have been sewn down around the neck and over the breast pocket. Along the bottom of the gown on both sides have been sewn three lines of white thread in herringbone stitch which have been formed into tassels at each point at which strips join. The quality of the design and sewing is outstanding.
